prompt: Each fit reports 2(−ℓ) + 2k, where k counts the fitted parameters.
why: That's AIC: fit plus a penalty per parameter.

prompt: With 6,301 training days, one criterion penalizes each parameter by ln n ≈ 8.7 instead of 2.
why: BIC's penalty grows with sample size, so it favors simpler models more than AIC.

prompt: GJR-GARCH reduces to GARCH(1,1) when γ = 0, so you test 2(ℓ_GJR − ℓ_GARCH) against a chi-square with 1 degree of freedom.
why: A likelihood ratio test for nested models: the revised model is a strict extension.
trap: Kupiec is also an LR test, but over VaR breaches, not model fits.

prompt: Every richer model has a higher in-sample log-likelihood than the simpler one it extends.
why: Extra parameters can only help in-sample, so fair comparison needs a penalty (AIC/BIC) or a test.
trap: Out-of-sample checks are the other guard.

prompt: For GJR-GARCH-t, k = 6 counts μ, ω, α, γ, β and ν.
tells: k = 6 counts μ, ω, α, γ, β and ν
why: Counting parameters correctly matters for AIC and BIC, including μ even when it's estimated by the sample mean.

prompt: AIC prefers GJR-GARCH-t, while BIC prefers GJR-GARCH with normal errors.
why: BIC's heavier penalty can reject ν; check out-of-sample fit and VaR backtests to decide.
trap: Disagreement is information, not an error.
